result.summary:
Verdicts per lead. GREAT SPACES: ready after small fixes. The email is specific and honest, but paragraph 1 is a dense block, it never says we sell this, and "each enquiry" assumes Book Now leads to WhatsApp. SWAGAT: ready after the common edits. It is the strongest note because the observation is the Send WhatsApp message button itself. PARSHWANATH: ready after small fixes. It has the weakest premise fit, because nothing in their ads or on their site is WhatsApp, so the page h1 and video say "WhatsApp enquiry from your ads" and the email says "each enquiry". Use the WhatsApp-hold rule for this lead. SPACE AGE: ready after small fixes. It is the only email that says what we do, but the subject is cut off on a phone and the non-affiliation sentence interrupts the hook. Pass-1 fixes check out. The project and brand names match the fact-check, no email says "your ads", "free" or "instant", the wording is soft, and no staff names appear. The Space Age {{2}} = "Arvind Sensora" versus a page "made for Space Age Consultants" is a known trade-off and I left it alone.

Email plus WhatsApp the same day: acceptable only as an email-first sequence. Send the email at about 10:30 to 11:30 and the WhatsApp 3 to 4 hours later, at about 3 to 4 PM. Skip the WhatsApp if the lead replied, clicked Try the demo, or wrote stop. The reason is that a cold WhatsApp from a +1 number with no warning is the message most likely to be blocked. Blocks and reports land on the only WABA (CAMPAIGN_PLAYBOOK line 22). A heads-up in the email lowers that risk, and the email promising an opt-out only works if a "stop" email is read before the WhatsApp slot.

Single change that most raises taps: split paragraph 1 into two short paragraphs, adding a one-line "what we do" sentence and dropping the four-item list. Exact text is in the per-lead findings.
